cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Let Them Keep Hope
cards.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Let's pack your paintings for the last gallery. You've finally picked up a brush again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If the big gallery rejected me too, I'm done. Did they write?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Their letter can wait. This gallery still needs your best three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pick them, then. I can't face another envelope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the envelopes. You finish the blue one; there's still somewhere for it to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's pack your paintings for the last gallery. You've finally picked up a brush again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If the big gallery rejected me too, I'm done. Did they write?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their letter can wait. This gallery still needs your best three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pick them, then. I can't face another envelope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the envelopes. You finish the blue one; there's still somewhere for it to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the seed packets. The allotment letter says we're on the waiting list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've covered our number. If it's another year indoors, I'm giving up gardening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The important bit is we're on it. Let's start tomatoes on my windowsill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll get tired of them before we get a plot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my sunny room. I'll move the bed; keep the packets.

cards.title: Admit You’re Hurt
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. When Mum cancelled our birthday dinner, were you disappointed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. I'd like your answer before I give mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I cried in the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. I told the cashier the birthday candles were seasonal allergies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I cried in the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did the boss calling us office furniture hurt you?

beats.speaker: B

cards.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.
